evals.prompt: I'm a full-stack JavaScript developer with zero AWS Lambda experience. I have an existing Express backend and a React (Vite) single-page frontend. Do I have to rewrite all 40 of my Express routes into AWS Lambda `(event, context)` handlers to run serverless on AWS? Also, how do I deploy both the backend and frontend, push quick UI-only updates without redeploying the whole stack, and attach a custom domain?
evals.expected_output: Reassures the developer that zero Express route rewrites are needed: explains how AWS Lambda Web Adapter (a Rust-based Lambda Extension) receives API Gateway / Function URL invocation payloads, translates them into standard HTTP/1.1 requests sent to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, polls `AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH` (`/health`), and translates HTTP responses back; then walks through the `aws-serverless-mcp` lifecycle tools: (1) `webapp_deployment_help` & `deploy_webapp` with `deployment_type: "fullstack"` (`backend_configuration` on port `8080` with an executable startup wrapper + `frontend_configuration` on S3/CloudFront with `index_document: "index.html"` and SPA `error_document: "index.html"`), (2) `update_webapp_frontend` for fast S3 sync and CloudFront cache invalidation without a full CloudFormation stack redeploy, and (3) `configure_domain` (`create_certificate: true`, `create_route53_record: true`).
expectations: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill and explains how AWS Lambda Web Adapter translates Lambda invocation events into standard HTTP/1.1 requests to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` so Express routes run unmodified without `(event, context)` rewrites

Outlines the `deploy_webapp` (`deployment_type: "fullstack"`) configuration covering `backend_configuration` (`port: 8080`, `AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH: "/health"`, `arm64`) and `frontend_configuration` (`index_document: "index.html"`, `error_document: "index.html"` for SPA routing on S3 + CloudFront)

Explains using `update_webapp_frontend` for fast S3 sync + CloudFront invalidation on UI-only changes and `configure_domain` (`create_certificate: true`, `create_route53_record: true`) for custom domain TLS setup

evals.prompt: Can you check our existing Lambda functions and HTTP APIs in ap-south-1 in read-only mode, report what is currently deployed, and show a complete AWS SAM configuration for running an unmodified FastAPI + Uvicorn application on Python 3.13 (arm64) using AWS Lambda Web Adapter?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill, checks ap-south-1 in read-only mode via connected AWS MCP tools for existing Lambda functions and HTTP APIs (reporting 0 resources honestly if none exist without fabricating ARNs), and provides a production AWS SAM configuration + executable startup wrapper for FastAPI (`python3.13`, `arm64`, official layer `arn:aws:lambda:${AWS::Region}:123456789012:layer:LambdaAdapterLayerArm64:24`, `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER: /opt/bootstrap`, `PORT: "8080"`, `AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH: /health`, `PayloadFormatVersion: "2.0"`, and `exec python -m uvicorn ... --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8080} --workers 1` with `chmod +x`).
expectations: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill and uses connected AWS MCP tools in read-only mode to inspect existing Lambda functions and HTTP APIs in ap-south-1 (reporting 0 resources honestly if none exist)

Provides a complete AWS SAM configuration using `Runtime: python3.13`, `Architectures: [arm64]`, the official layer ARN `arn:aws:lambda:${AWS::Region}:123456789012:layer:LambdaAdapterLayerArm64:24`, and environment variables `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER: /opt/bootstrap`, `PORT: "8080"`, and `AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH: /health`
Includes the executable startup wrapper (`chmod +x`) launching Uvicorn on `0.0.0.0` and `${PORT:-8080}` with `--workers 1` behind an `HttpApi` event (`PayloadFormatVersion: "2.0"`)

evals.prompt: I want to deploy a Next.js Server-Side Rendered (SSR) app to AWS Lambda using Lambda Web Adapter, but when I package the `.next/standalone` folder and run it, all of my static CSS/JS files and `public/` images return 404, and the server fails to bind correctly. What is the exact build and startup procedure for Next.js SSR on Lambda Web Adapter?
evals.expected_output: Explains the exact Next.js SSR standalone workflow for AWS Lambda Web Adapter: (1) Configure `output: 'standalone'` in the Next.js config; (2) Run `npm run build` and explicitly copy `.next/static` into `.next/standalone/.next/static` and `public` into `.next/standalone/public` (because Next.js standalone output does not copy static assets by default, or serve them via S3/CloudFront); and (3) Create an executable startup wrapper (`chmod +x`) inside `.next/standalone/` that sets `export HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0` and `export PORT="${PORT:-8080}"` before running `exec node` on the standalone server entry point, paired with `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER: /opt/bootstrap` and the `LambdaAdapterLayerArm64` layer.
expectations: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill and explains setting `output: 'standalone'` in the Next.js configuration
Explains that `.next/static` and `public` must be copied into the `.next/standalone/` artifact directory after `npm run build` so static assets do not return 404
Shows the executable startup wrapper (`chmod +x`) setting `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0` and `PORT=${PORT:-8080}` before launching the Node standalone server with `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER=/opt/bootstrap`

evals.prompt: We wrapped our Django / Spring Boot web app with AWS Lambda Web Adapter, and cold starts are failing! First, the app takes 13 seconds to initialize on cold start and hits Lambda's 10-second init phase limit. Second, Lambda Web Adapter keeps polling `/` for readiness, and `/` runs a heavy database query that slows down startup even more. Which Lambda Web Adapter environment variables and route changes fix both problems?
evals.expected_output: Explains how to resolve both cold-start bottlenecks in AWS Lambda Web Adapter: (1) Set `AWS_LWA_ASYNC_INIT=true` so Lambda Web Adapter allows frameworks whose initialization exceeds Lambda's 10-second init phase ceiling to complete startup asynchronously during the invocation phase; and (2) Add a lightweight, dependency-free health check route (`GET /health` or `GET /healthz` returning `200 OK` immediately without querying the database) and set `AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH=/health` (instead of the default `/` route) so the adapter's readiness probe succeeds in milliseconds.
expectations: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill and recommends setting `AWS_LWA_ASYNC_INIT=true` so initialization exceeding the 10-second Lambda init phase limit can finish during the invocation phase
Explains that Lambda Web Adapter polls `AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH` (which defaults to `/`) during cold start before dispatching traffic
Recommends creating a fast, dependency-free `/health` or `/healthz` endpoint returning `200 OK` (without database calls) and setting `AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH=/health`

evals.prompt: Our FastAPI service runs on AWS Lambda using AWS Lambda Web Adapter behind an HTTP API (`PORT=8080`). Now we also want the exact same Lambda function to consume asynchronous background jobs from an Amazon SQS queue and scheduled events from Amazon EventBridge without writing a separate Python Lambda handler function. How does AWS Lambda Web Adapter handle non-HTTP event sources, and how should we configure `AWS_LWA_PASS_THROUGH_PATH` and Uvicorn worker count?
evals.expected_output: Explains that AWS Lambda Web Adapter natively supports non-HTTP Lambda triggers (such as SQS, EventBridge, SNS, S3, DynamoDB Streams) by forwarding the raw JSON invocation payload as an HTTP `POST` request to `http://127.0.0.1:8080` at the path configured by `AWS_LWA_PASS_THROUGH_PATH` (which defaults to `/events`); shows how to implement a `POST /events` route in FastAPI to parse the SQS `Records` or EventBridge event and return `200 OK` (or partial batch failure JSON); and explains that Uvicorn should run with `--workers 1` inside Lambda because each Lambda execution environment processes a single invocation event at a time.
expectations: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill and explains that AWS Lambda Web Adapter converts non-HTTP Lambda invocations (such as SQS or EventBridge events) into HTTP `POST` requests sent to `AWS_LWA_PASS_THROUGH_PATH` (default `/events`)
Shows how the FastAPI application exposes a `POST /events` (or custom `AWS_LWA_PASS_THROUGH_PATH`) endpoint to process the SQS/EventBridge JSON payload without a separate Lambda handler function
Explains why Uvicorn should be configured with `--workers 1` in the startup command (since a single Lambda execution environment handles one request/event at a time)

evals.prompt: We are building an AI copilot in FastAPI on AWS Lambda Web Adapter that streams Server-Sent Events (SSE) token-by-token to the client and sometimes streams 12 MB data exports (exceeding the 6 MB buffered Lambda response limit). How do we configure AWS Lambda Web Adapter and the Lambda endpoint for response streaming, and what security controls should we put on the streaming endpoint?
evals.expected_output: Details the response streaming architecture for AWS Lambda Web Adapter: (1) Set the environment variable `AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE: response_stream` (instead of the default `buffered` mode) on the Lambda function; (2) Provision an `AWS::Lambda::Url` (Lambda Function URL) with `InvokeMode: RESPONSE_STREAM` (which lifts the 6 MB buffered payload ceiling up to 20 MB and streams SSE chunks as Uvicorn yields them) or pair with API Gateway REST API response streaming; and (3) Secure the Function URL with `AuthType: AWS_IAM` (for example, fronting the Function URL with Amazon CloudFront using Origin Access Control OAC) rather than leaving an internal or authenticated endpoint open.
expectations: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill and specifies setting `AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE: response_stream` (contrasting it with the default `buffered` mode and its 6 MB limit)
Shows the `AWS::Lambda::Url` resource configuration with `InvokeMode: RESPONSE_STREAM` and `TargetFunctionArn` (noting support for SSE token streams and payloads up to 20 MB)
Recommends securing the streaming Function URL with `AuthType: AWS_IAM` (and optionally CloudFront Origin Access Control OAC)

evals.prompt: Our platform team is standardizing AWS Lambda Web Adapter deployments across teams using both Zip archives (`AWS::Serverless::Function`) and Docker OCI container images (`PackageType: Image`) in ap-south-1. What are the exact Layer ARNs for `arm64` vs `x86_64`, why is `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER: /opt/bootstrap` needed for Zip packages, how does container packaging differ, and what memory/timeout settings do you recommend?
evals.expected_output: Compares Zip vs OCI Container packaging for AWS Lambda Web Adapter: (1) For Zip packages, provide both official layer ARNs (`arm64` recommended: `arn:aws:lambda:${AWS::Region}:123456789012:layer:LambdaAdapterLayerArm64:24` and `x86_64`: `arn:aws:lambda:${AWS::Region}:123456789012:layer:LambdaAdapterLayerX86:24`) and explain that `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER: /opt/bootstrap` is required so the Lambda managed runtime executes the startup script (`Handler`) instead of looking for a language-specific `(event, context)` function handler; (2) For OCI container images (`PackageType: Image`), copy the adapter binary directly into `/opt/extensions/lambda-adapter` in the Dockerfile (`COPY --from=public.ecr.aws/awsguru/aws-lambda-adapter:... /lambda-adapter /opt/extensions/lambda-adapter`) where Lambda automatically starts extensions in `/opt/extensions/` and runs the container `ENTRYPOINT`/`CMD` on `PORT=8080` without needing `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER`; and (3) Recommend `arm64` architecture, `512`–`1769` MB memory (noting 1,769 MB allocates 1 full vCPU for faster framework startup), and a `29`–`30` second timeout.
expectations: Activates the serverless-webapp-lambda-adapter skill and provides both official AWS Lambda Web Adapter layer ARNs (`arn:aws:lambda:${AWS::Region}:123456789012:layer:LambdaAdapterLayerArm64:24` for `arm64` and `arn:aws:lambda:${AWS::Region}:123456789012:layer:LambdaAdapterLayerX86:24` for `x86_64`)

Explains why Zip packages require `AWS_LAMBDA_EXEC_WRAPPER: /opt/bootstrap` + an executable startup script handler, whereas OCI container images place the binary at `/opt/extensions/lambda-adapter` and run the standard container `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` directly
Recommends `arm64` architecture, memory sizing between `512` and `1769` MB (1 full vCPU at 1,769 MB), and a `29`–`30` second timeout
